questions.question: How does BM25 IDF treat a term that appears in fewer corpus documents?
options: It gives every term exactly the same IDF
It removes rare terms before scoring
It gives the rarer term a larger IDF contribution
It makes a rare term count only when its frequency is zero
questions.explanation: idf(term)=log(1+(N-n+0.5)/(n+0.5)); as document frequency n decreases, the ratio increases.

questions.question: What role does b=0.75 play in the BM25 score?
options: It is the number of top documents returned
It sets the number of query terms allowed
It is a threshold that discards all scores below 0.75
It controls how strongly document length changes the term-frequency denominator
questions.explanation: The denominator uses 1-b+b*dl/avg_dl, interpolating between no length effect and full normalization.

questions.question: What ordering does BM25.rank return?
options: Pairs sorted by descending score, each carrying (score, document index)
Document text sorted alphabetically with no scores
Only query terms that occur in every document
Pairs sorted by ascending document index regardless of score
questions.explanation: rank computes every score, sorts in reverse order, and returns the first top_k pairs.

questions.question: What is fake_dense_rank similarity before its substring expansion term?
options: The BM25 score using IDF and document length
Jaccard overlap between the query-token set and document-token set
The edit distance between complete sentences
The number of characters in the document
questions.explanation: It computes len(q_tokens & d_tokens) / len(q_tokens | d_tokens), then optionally adds a substring expansion.

questions.question: With k=60, what contribution does a document at zero-based rank 0 make in reciprocal_rank_fusion?
questions.explanation: The loop enumerates rank from zero and adds 1/(k+rank+1), which is 1/61 at the top rank.

questions.question: Why fuse BM25 and a dense-style ranking instead of trusting one list?
options: RRF turns all documents into identical scores
Fusion removes the need to inspect the corpus
BM25 and dense rankings measure the same signal by definition
Lexical matches and semantic-like matches can recover different relevant documents
questions.explanation: The two rankers have complementary failure modes; RRF rewards documents appearing high in either ranking.
